summary.text: A 36-year-old woman with idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura diagnosed at age 29 years and treated with oral prednisolone, previous cesarean section and an in vitro fertilization pregnancy had intrauterine fetal death after 24 weeks of pregnancy. On admission she was diagnosed with preeclampsia (blood pressure 160/123 mmHg, albuminuria, generalized edema) with a platelet count of 5000/μL.

She received 20 units of platelets and oral prednisolone 20 mg, then underwent emergency cesarean section under general anesthesia, without intraoperative respiratory or hemodynamic dysfunction. Pre-operative chest radiograph showed pleural effusion without pulmonary edema, the electrocardiogram showed sinus rhythm without ST-T changes, and C-reactive protein and creatine kinase were within the normal range.

After extubation she developed respiratory distress with sinus tachycardia and an SpO2 decrease to 91%, and was transferred to the intensive care unit and started on noninvasive positive pressure ventilation. Chest radiograph showed butterfly shadows with a cardiothoracic ratio of 57.1%, and echocardiography showed an ejection fraction of 20% with diffuse severe hypokinesis, leading to a diagnosis of peripartum cardiomyopathy.

She was treated with intravenous milrinone, oral bromocriptine 5 mg/day and enalapril maleate, with rapid improvement and a move to the general ward on the second postoperative day. Milrinone was stopped on the fourth postoperative day and bromocriptine was later reduced and discontinued. Ejection fraction was 57% fourteen days after surgery, and she was discharged 24 days after surgery without further complications.
